Source: Android NetworkStatsManager. Some phones keep only limited history, and mobile totals may be unavailable on Android 9 and older.
Uses Android\'s local VPN feature to cut off internet for apps you choose. Nothing is sent to any server.
Block at least one app below, then turn the firewall on.
The firewall was stopped by Android or another VPN app took over. Blocked apps can use the internet again.
VPN permission was not granted. The firewall needs it to work.

Only the apps you block are routed into a local, on-device VPN. Their traffic is dropped, so those apps lose internet while the rule is active. Other apps are not affected. Wi-Fi rules also apply to Ethernet. Android allows only one VPN at a time, so another VPN app will turn this firewall off.
DevicePilot does not forward, record or inspect any traffic. Packets from blocked apps are discarded on the device.
Android\'s thermal status API requires Android 10 or newer. Battery temperature is still shown.
Reported by Android: 1.0 means severe throttling is expected.
Pause games, video recording or navigation, unplug the charger, remove a thick case and let the phone cool down in a shaded place.
Collecting readings while this screen is open…
History is kept only in memory while DevicePilot is running.
Your device does not let apps read CPU/GPU thermal sensors. DevicePilot does not use root and does not guess these values.
Source: Linux thermal zones (/sys/class/thermal). Names come from the device kernel; the type label is a best guess from the name.
There is no single safe temperature for every phone. Android\'s thermal status is the most reliable signal for your device.
Source: BatteryManager. Current and charge values depend on the manufacturer and may be missing.

• Lower screen brightness or use adaptive brightness.
• Restrict background battery use for apps you rarely open.
• Turn on battery saver when you need more time.
• Avoid charging in hot places.
Lifespan estimates are not shown because Android does not give apps a reliable measurement of battery wear.

Source: ActivityManager.MemoryInfo. Android keeps recently used apps in RAM on purpose, so high usage is normal.
Checks memory and storage and clears DevicePilot\'s own cache. It does not kill other apps — Android manages them and restarting them often uses more battery.

Android no longer lets regular apps see or stop other apps\' processes. To stop a misbehaving app, open App management and use Force stop, or view Running services in Developer options.

Shorter animations make the phone feel quicker, but they do not make the processor faster. You change these settings yourself — DevicePilot cannot change protected settings.
More ways to keep your phone fast
Keep at least 10–15% of storage free.
Uninstall apps you no longer use.
Restrict background battery use for rarely used apps.
Review apps with high data usage.
Remove unnecessary widgets and live wallpapers.
Use your manufacturer\'s performance mode if available.
Avoid intensive use when the phone is overheating.
Restart the phone if problems persist.

DevicePilot helps you understand and manage your Android device using only official Android features. It works offline, needs no account and collects no analytics.
DevicePilot has no backend, no login, no ads and no analytics. Everything runs on your phone.
Only your settings (theme, units, alerts), firewall rules and the list of APK files you added are saved, in the app\'s private storage on this device. Uninstalling DevicePilot deletes them.
If you allow Usage Access, app usage time, data usage and app sizes are read to display them. They are never uploaded or shared.
The firewall uses Android\'s VpnService only on the device. Traffic of blocked apps is discarded; no traffic is forwarded to a server, logged or inspected.
Files are accessed only when you pick them with the system file picker. Nothing is deleted without your confirmation.
Installs and uninstalls always go through Android\'s own confirmation screens. DevicePilot cannot act silently.
See RAM, storage, battery and Android\'s thermal status — with the source of every number.
Search apps, install APKs safely and uninstall what you don\'t need through Android\'s own screens.
Block internet access for chosen apps with a local, on-device VPN. No traffic leaves through DevicePilot.
Track battery temperature and Android\'s thermal warnings, and learn how to cool your phone down.
No account, no tracking. DevicePilot asks for each permission only when you use the feature that needs it.
This phone does not share cycle count or capacity with apps (Android 14+ reports cycles on most phones).
This copy of DevicePilot was changed by someone else. Please install the original app from the official source.
Time since the phone was last started (restarted or switched on).
Since Android 10, Android does not let apps read the IMEI. Tap below to see it in the phone dialer (*#06#).
Allow Phone permission for SIM details
Charging power = battery voltage × current while plugged in. Android does not expose the phone\'s maximum supported wattage; the charger value appears only when the device reports it.
See apps with active background services or recent activity, close them, or switch their internet off.
Android shows which apps run in the background only to apps with Usage Access. Turn it on for DevicePilot.
Based on Android\'s activity log (last 12 hours)
Android will close the cached background processes of these apps. Apps showing a notification (a running service) or on screen keep running, and Android may restart apps later.
No background services or recently active apps were found.
Firewall is off — tap to turn it on so this takes effect

Android 8 and later do not let regular apps list or kill other apps\' processes directly. \"Close\" uses Android\'s official request to close cached processes; \"Force stop\" opens Android\'s own Force stop button.
DevicePilot needs these to show complete information. Each one is used only for the feature described.
Special permissions open an Android settings screen — turn the switch on for DevicePilot and come back. You can change them anytime in Settings › Permissions.
For optional alerts: overheating, low storage, data limit and firewall status.
Shows running apps, data usage per app, screen time and app sizes.
Lets you install APK files. Android still asks you to confirm every install.
Lets the on-device firewall block internet for apps you choose. No traffic leaves the phone.
I have read and agree to the Privacy Policy and Disclaimer.
Your data stays on your phone
If you allow the Phone permission, SIM state and carrier names are read only to show them on the Device details page. They are never stored or sent anywhere.
No data is collected or shared with third parties. No data is transmitted off the device. Data stored locally can be removed by clearing app data or uninstalling.
DevicePilot is an independent app. Android, Google Play and related marks are trademarks of Google LLC. DevicePilot is not endorsed by or affiliated with Google or any phone manufacturer.
Values are read from Android and your device\'s hardware. Some phones report incomplete or inaccurate values. The health score and suggestions are guidance only.
DevicePilot does not claim to free RAM, clean junk or speed up the processor. Any change you make in system settings is your decision.
Installing APK files from unknown sources can harm your device. Only install files you trust. Android shows its own confirmation for every install and uninstall.
The firewall uses Android\'s VPN feature. Android allows only one VPN at a time, and Android or another VPN app can turn it off. Blocked apps lose internet while a rule is active.
